extracted.intended_audience: power companies, state regulators, industry stakeholders, environmental and public interest groups, and EPA staff involved in CAA section 111 rulemaking and state plan development
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register preamble finalizing CAA section 111 actions regulating greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs), including BSER determinations, emission guidelines for existing units, and NSPS for new/reconstructed/modified units. Includes compliance deadlines, subcategories, reliability and environmental justice considerations, and state plan requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER) determination under CAA section 111
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA must determine the 'best system of emission reduction . . . adequately demonstrated' taking into account the cost of the reductions, non-air quality health and environmental impacts, and energy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key features include that it must reduce emissions, be based on 'adequately demonstrated' technology, and have a reasonable cost of control. The BSER may be forward-looking (EPA may determine a control is 'adequately demonstrated' even if new and not yet in widespread commercial use) and the most relevant costs are costs to the regulated facility. EPA may subcategorize sources when different sets of sources have different characteristics relevant to BSER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of emission limitation determination and distinction between new and existing sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Once EPA identifies the BSER, it must determine the 'degree of emission limitation' achievable by application of the BSER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For new sources, EPA establishes a standard of performance reflecting that degree of emission limitation. For existing sources, EPA includes information concerning the BSER and associated degree of emission limitation in emission guidelines and directs the states to adopt state plans containing standards of performance consistent with the emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategorization of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may determine that different sets of sources have different characteristics relevant for determining the BSER and may subcategorize sources accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories allow different BSER determinations and standards of performance where source characteristics (e.g., fuel type, capacity factor, anticipated retirement) differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of ACE Rule — adequacy and specificity standard
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA concludes the suite of heat rate improvements identified in the ACE Rule is not an appropriate BSER for existing coal-fired EGUs and that the ACE Rule conflicted with CAA section 111 because it did not provide sufficient specificity as to the BSER or the 'degree of emission limitation achievable though application of the [BSER].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACE's rejection of CCS and natural gas co-firing as BSER was based on reasons that no longer apply; EPA is withdrawing ACE-related proposed NSR revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for existing coal-fired steam generating units (CCS 90% capture)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing CCS with 90 percent capture as BSER for existing coal-fired steam generating units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These units have a presumptive standard of an 88.4 percent reduction in annual emission rate, with a compliance deadline of January 1, 2032. EPA finds CCS is adequately demonstrated and cost-reasonable given declining costs and tax credits (e.g., IRC section 45Q).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-lived subcategory for coal units planning to permanently cease by 2039 (co-firing BSER)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalizes a separate subcategory for existing coal-fired steam generating units that demonstrate they plan to permanently cease operation before January 1, 2039.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BSER for this subcategory is co-firing with natural gas at a level of 40 percent of the unit's annual heat input, with a presumptive standard corresponding to a 16 percent reduction in annual emission rate and a compliance deadline of January 1, 2030.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability exemption for units retiring before January 1, 2032
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing an applicability exemption for existing coal-fired steam EGUs demonstrating that they plan to permanently cease operation prior to January 1, 2032.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA determined units retiring before this date generally do not have cost-reasonable options for improving GHG emissions performance; such sources will not be subject to these emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER and presumptive standards for existing natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing routine methods of operation and maintenance as the BSER for intermediate load and base load natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units, and finalizing presumptive standards for various load categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumptive standards: base load (>45% capacity factor) — 1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross; intermediate load (>8% to ≤45%) — 1,600 lb CO2/MWh-gross. For low load (<8% capacity factor), EPA finalizes a uniform fuels BSER and presumptive input-based standard of 170 lb CO2/MMBtu for oil-fired sources and 130 lb CO2/MMBtu for natural gas-fired sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSPS subcategories for new and reconstructed combustion turbines (base/intermediate/low)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing emission standards for three subcategories of combustion turbines—base load, intermediate load, and low load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BSER differs by subcategory (see separate criteria): base load includes highly efficient generation plus CCS 90% (two-phase implementation), intermediate load is highly efficient simple cycle generation, low load is use of lower-emitting fuels.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for base load combustion turbines — two-component approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The BSER for base load combustion turbines includes two components to be implemented initially in two phases: (1) highly efficient generation and (2) utilization of CCS with 90 percent capture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizing lead time for CCS and infrastructure, EPA finalized a second phase compliance deadline of January 1, 2032 for the CCS component.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for intermediate load combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has identified highly efficient simple cycle generation as the BSER for intermediate load combustion turbines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects reliance on improved unit efficiency rather than CCS for mid-capacity-factor turbines.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for low load combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing that the BSER for low load combustion turbines is the use of lower-emitting fuels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable to turbines with low annual capacity factors where fuel switching is the most appropriate emission-reducing option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for large modifications of coal-fired steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing revisions to the standards of performance for coal-fired steam generating units that undertake a large modification (increase in hourly emission rate >10%) to mirror the emission guidelines for existing coal-fired steam generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents creating an unjustified disparity between emission control obligations for modified and existing coal-fired steam EGUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: No current revision of NSPS for newly constructed/reconstructed steam EGUs (monitoring posture)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not revising the NSPS for newly constructed or reconstructed fossil fuel-fired steam EGUs at this time but will continue to consider whether to review the 2015 NSPS in light of new developments (e.g., possible new coal plant in Alaska).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA may determine either to conduct a review and propose revised standards or not, as warranted by developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of rule components
rubrics_metrics.description: The final action is composed of four independent rules and EPA intends that each rule (and many internal components/subcategories) is severable from the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA explains how each sub-rule and many subcomponents can function sensibly independently (e.g., BSERs and standards for different subcategories stand on their own).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grid reliability accommodations and mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA made multiple adjustments to ensure requirements can be implemented without compromising resource adequacy and grid reliability, based on stakeholder input and consultation with reliability entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments include changes to the universe of affected sources, longer compliance timeframes for CCS implementation, and compliance flexibilities; articulation of appropriate use of RULOF during state plan development and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term reliability emergency mechanisms and alternative emission limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: For existing fossil fuel-fired EGUs (and similarly for new sources), a short-term reliability emergency mechanism is available for states to provide more flexibility by using an alternative emission limitation during acute operational emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to address acute strain on the grid; available subject to criteria in state plans and EPA oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year compliance date extensions and reliability assurance mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: States may provide a compliance date extension for existing sources of up to 1 year under certain circumstances for sources installing control technologies, and may include a reliability assurance mechanism of up to 1 year to allow units that planned to cease operating to temporarily remain available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any extensions exceeding 1 year must be addressed through a state plan revision. To utilize these reliability pathways there must be an adequate demonstration of need and certification by a reliability authority and approval by the appropriate EPA Regional Administrator. EPA plans to seek FERC's advice for extension requests exceeding 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year extension pathway for new baseload combustion turbines' CCS compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: For new fossil fuel-fired combustion turbines, the EPA is creating a mechanism whereby baseload units may request a 1-year extension of their CCS compliance deadline under certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flexibility recognizing potential deployment and infrastructure timing constraints for new units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost and technological trend considerations in BSER determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA considered recent declines in CCS costs, Federal tax incentives (e.g., IRC section 45Q), funding from IIJA and CHIPS, industry announcements, and fleet retirement trends when concluding CCS is adequately demonstrated and cost-reasonable for certain subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes CCS capital expenditures are significant and cost-reasonableness depends on expected unit operation; incentives and declining costs support EPA's conclusion that CCS is BSER in appropriate cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice (EJ) analytic and outreach requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with Executive Order 14096 and EPA commitments, EPA carefully considered impacts on communities with environmental justice concerns and conducted extensive outreach including Tribal nations and communities with EJ concerns during rule development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EJ considerations are integrated into regulatory development; EPA used stakeholder outreach to inform rule decisions and analysis (see section XII.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource adequacy analysis and modeling requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA evaluated resource adequacy implications of the actions in the final technical support document (TSD), Resource Adequacy Analysis, and conducted capacity expansion modeling that accounts for resource adequacy needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA performed sensitivity analyses (e.g., higher load growth) and modeled a compliant scenario that meets resource adequacy, finding that resource adequacy can be maintained with final rules. This analysis informs flexibility and timing adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of proposed NSR revisions associated with ACE Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is withdrawing the proposed revisions to the New Source Review (NSR) regulations that were included with the ACE Rule proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This withdrawal is part of the repeal of ACE and associated regulatory changes addressed separately.
